title: R' Abba bar Aha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman writes that we find that he always spoke in the name of Rabbi. In Berakhot ch. 1, halakhah 6 [Yerushalmi], R. Abba bar Aha said there in the name of Rabbi: if one did not mention the covenant in [the blessing for] the Land, or did not mention the kingdom of the House of David in [the blessing] "Who builds Jerusalem," they make him repeat it. And in [Bavli] Berakhot 49a the reading is: "R. Yaakov bar Aha said in the name of Rabbeinu." Hyman suggests that it should be corrected to match the Yerushalmi and reports that this is the reading of Yuchasin. And in Berakhot ch. 3, halakhah 4 [Yerushalmi]: R. Abba bar Aha, in the name of Rabbeinu: one who studies halakhot but does not study aggadot. And in [Bavli] Berakhot 22a the reading is: "R. Aha bar Yaakov said in the name of Rabbeinu" (Hyman reports that Rashi explains: Rav). Hyman reports that the reading of Yuchasin, of Dikdukei Soferim (ד"ק"ס) and Dikdukei Soferim is: "R. Ela said, R. Abba bar Aha said in the name of Rabbeinu." And in [Bavli] Berakhot 25b, according to Hyman’s report of the reading of Dikdukei Soferim (ד"ק"ס): "R. Elai said, R. Abba bar Aha said in the name of Rabbeinu: they taught it regarding muddy water." And in the Gemara: "Rabbi Elazar [supplied אר״א] said, and some say R. Aha bar Abba bar Aha, etc." And so we find in Shabbat ch. 1, end of halakhah 4 [Yerushalmi] that he spoke in the name of Rabbi. And in the old Midrash Tehillim ch. 107 [supplied ch. 107]: "R. Abahu bar Aha in the name of Rabbeinu" — and Hyman says it should read R. Abba. And there in ch. 14 he spoke in the name of R. Hanin, and Hyman says it should read in the name of Rabbeinu.

Hyman writes that what remains to us from him is his precious saying, [Yerushalmi] Shekalim, beginning of ch. 1: "You cannot fathom the character of this nation: they were asked [to give] for the Tabernacle and they gave; they were asked [to give] for the [golden] calf and they gave." (In the Bavli Shekalim there, Hyman calls the reading a mistake: R. Bibi bar Aha.) He is likewise mentioned in Nazir ch. 6, halakhah 2; Shemot Rabbah ch. 44, sec. 4; Midrash Tehillim ch. 78, sec. 17; and Hyman writes that we find that he went down to Babylonia, in Berakhot ch. 1, halakhah 6.

notes.text: Printed abbreviations (e.g., ד"ק"ס, "היוחסין", "ש"ר", "מד' תהלים") are not expanded by a supplied witness; expansions here follow ordinary conventions and are uncertain. The printed "ברכות כ" at the start of the sentence in p001 and "ברכות כ" in p002 appear to be a source oddity (possibly a stray letter before the citation) and were treated as a citation prefix; "ר' בא" is rendered as R. Abba per context.

Hyman's own corrections ("וצ"ל") are rendered as he states them, preserving his conjectural attributions, including his proposed emendations of R. Yaakov bar Aha, R. Aha bar Yaakov, R. Abahu bar Aha, R. Hanin, and R. Bibi bar Aha.

Whole source/all notes reviewed. Beginning-of-Shekalimchapter1 (רפ״א) restored against incorrect endofchapter1. Rabbi remains source title, without the draft’s unsupplied YehudahHaNasi identification; source’s Rabbi/Rabbeinu/RashiRav distinctions preserved. Hyman owns every proposed Abba/Aha/Abahu/Hanin/Bibi substitution and manuscript-reading report; not canonical identity or correction-history proof. Source itself writes דק״ס and full דקדוקי סופרים consecutively, so the contextual work expansion is disclosed, not prohibited by an empty registry. Reported BavliShekalim is Hyman’s designation, not a newly asserted independent Babylonian tractate. אר״א abbreviated speaker remains literal R.A. and held. Citation-prefix כ is not automatically a stray source letter. All inherited notes retained with these qualifications. References to printed/native readings in inherited notes are preserved historical claims; this root pass uses supplied digital text and named saved editions, not a fresh pixel or correction-history verification.

The whole saved Davidson Berakhot 25b paragraph explicitly names Rabbi Elazar before the alternative Rabbi Acha bar Abba bar Acha, followed by “in the name of Rabbeinu” and the muddy-water clause. This locally supports expanding the supplied אר״א as Rabbi Elazar, while keeping that supplied acronym visible. It does not identify Rabbeinu with Rabbi or Rav across the entry. The digital paragraph titles the alternative Acha, but not either father in that chain; Hyman’s abbreviated R. titles elsewhere remain unexpanded. The catalog heading’s abbreviated title is likewise rendered R' Abba; no full title is transferred to him from the distinct Acha alternative. Hyman’s ALWAYS statement, Rabbi/Rabbeinu distinctions, his report of Rashi’s Rav explanation, Yuchasin and repeated דק״ס/Dikdukei Soferim readings, and every “should read” remain attributed to him. His “Bavli Shekalim” designation, beginning-of-chapter locator, valuable saying and inference of descent to Babylonia are retained as his account; no fresh collation of those other named texts or apparatus was performed here. The current three mixed notes remain verbatim, and the p001 source hold remains in place. No Hebrew repair, printed correction history, identity, teacher or chronology binding is admitted.

In the consulted Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:6, Ba son of R’ Aha quotes Rabbi on the covenant and Davidic kingship. The Davidson Berakhot 49a chain has R’ Ilea report R’ Yaakov bar Aha in Rabbeinu’s name. In Yerushalmi Berakhot 3:4 and Shabbat 1:4, Abba or Ba bar Aha quotes Rabbi on studying halakhot and aggadot. Hyman gives Rabbeinu in his Berakhot 3:4 citation. Davidson Berakhot 22a instead has R’ Ilai report R’ Aha bar Yaakov in Rabbeinu’s name, and Rashi locally glosses Rabbeinu as Rav. At Davidson Berakhot 25b, Rabbi Elazar and the alternative Rabbi Acha bar Abba bar Acha appear in the muddy-water passage. Hyman’s Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim readings and proposed emendations remain his reports. His printed notice (I, p. 15) has the abbreviation דק״ס and gives the old Midrash Tehillim chapter 107 marker once, beside the longer supplied wording. His Shekalim quotation has the Tabernacle before the calf. In both named Yerushalmi witnesses, Ba bar Aha gives the calf first and the Tabernacle second. Hyman’s “Bavli Shekalim” label and Bibi reading remain his report. The Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:6 wording says he went down “there” and observed the practice. Hyman understands “there” as Babylonia.
